## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Samiddhijātaka* (Ja 167) is a narrative belonging to the Pali Jātaka collection [SuttaCentral; Fausböll 1879]. According to the traditional framework, the Buddha related this discourse while staying at the Tapoda Park (Tapodārāma) near Rājagaha, occasioned by the Elder Samiddhi [SuttaCentral; Fausböll 1879]. In the story of the present, Samiddhi spends the entire night striving in meditation, bathes at dawn in the Tapoda hot springs, and stands drying his limbs clad in an undergarment [Bhikkhu Bodhi 2003; Fausböll 1879]. A female spirit (*devadhītā* or earth-deity), captivated by his youthful beauty, approaches and urges him to enjoy worldly and sensual pleasures before old age rather than renouncing without enjoying [Rhys Davids 1917; Bhikkhu Bodhi 2003]. In the story of the past, the Bodhisatta was an ascetic in an identical situation who addressed the goddess with Dhamma teachings, prompting her disappearance; the Buddha concludes the Jātaka by identifying himself as that ancient ascetic [Fausböll 1879]. The opening verse begins with the refrain *Abhutvā bhikkhasi bhikkhu* [SuttaCentral; Fausböll 1879].

### Parallels and Text Reuse
The narrative and poetic core of the *Samiddhijātaka* corresponds directly to the *Samiddhisutta* (SN 1.20) in the *Devatāsaṁyutta* [SuttaCentral; Holz; Bhikkhu Bodhi 2003]. Modern scholars note that the verses in SN 1.20 are virtually verbatim identical with those in the *Samiddhijātaka*, sharing the same narrative plot with minor diction differences—such as the Jātaka explicitly identifying the spirit as a *devadhītā* [Rhys Davids 1917; Bhikkhu Bodhi 2003]. Automatically computed text-reuse data from DharmaNexus confirms this connection, identifying close shared passages between Ja 167 (§0.4–2.4) and SN 1 (§20.9.3–20.12.4), alongside recurring prose and verse alignments with the commentary in the *Jātaka-aṭṭhakathā* [DharmaNexus].
**Parallels and text reuse**

- Passage-level parallels (SuttaCentral): SN 1.20 Samiddhisutta
- Text reuse within the Pali corpus (DharmaNexus): Devatā Saṁyutta (SN 1) (§0.4–2.4 ↔ §20.9.3–20.12.4); Jātaka-aṭṭhakathā (Dutiyo bhāgo) (Atk S0513a2) (§0.4–1.4 ↔ §309–310)
